body.v: Your inbox is 99% full. Sign in within 1 hour or incoming mail will be rejected.

hotspots.explain: "cl0uddrive" has a zero where the o belongs, and it is not CloudDrive's domain, clouddrive.example, anyway.
"Dear user": a real service knows your name.
Who chose the one-hour deadline, you or them? A threat of missing mail is made to hurry you.
The button leads to cl0uddrive-support.example, a lookalike domain. A lookalike link can look perfectly reasonable when you hover over it.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone pretending to be CloudDrive. 'cl0uddrive' has a zero where the o belongs, and it is not CloudDrive's domain anyway.

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Fear and hurry: you are told mail will be lost unless you act within an hour.
choices: Fear of missing mail, with a one-hour rush
None: it is a routine notice

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Sign in through the link, which would give your login to the sender.

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Click nothing. Report it to IT, then check your mailbox by opening the official site yourself.
choices: Reply and ask if the message is genuine
Open the official site yourself and report the email
Hover over the link and sign in if it looks reasonable

actions.label: Click nothing, report it to IT, then open the official site yourself
actions.consequence: Your mailbox is fine. The email was fake and your report may protect a colleague.

actions.label: Sign in through the link, quickly
actions.consequence: The page looks like CloudDrive, but your login goes straight to the scammer.

actions.label: Reply and ask the sender whether the message is genuine
actions.consequence: The scammer says yes, of course. Your reply also shows your address is live.

actions.label: Hover over the link and sign in if the address looks reasonable
actions.consequence: A lookalike address can look reasonable. You gave your login away.

attacker_reveal: A zero instead of an o, and a clock ticking... You read the words, not the letters. People who are worried about their mail rarely check the sender.
